Webinar: Monitoring report: Emissions reduction (2025)

Is NZ on track to meet its emissions reductions goals? In this webinar, Chief Executive Jo Hendy and Project Director Rob Carr dive into the Climate Change Commission's latest report. This yearly report tracks the progress the country is making towards meeting its emissions budgets and the 2050 emissions reduction target.

The full report, summaries and technical documents are available on our website: https://www.climatecommission.govt.nz/erm-2025?utm_source=youtube.com&utm_campaign=erm-2025&utm_medium=social&utm_content=webinar

You can find today's presentation slides on our Webinars page: https://www.climatecommission.govt.nz/get-involved/watch/webinars?utm_source=youtube.com&utm_campaign=erm-2025&utm_medium=social&utm_content=webinar

Sign up to get alerts about our upcoming webinars: https://confirmsubscription.com/h/t/2DB84EBFF23E1BC9

Monitoring emissions reductions 2025: Is NZ on track?

The Climate Change Commission's annual report tracking Aotearoa New Zealand's progress on climate change budgets and targets is out now – so is the country on track in 2025? Chief Executive Jo Hendy shares some top takeaways from the report.

Our new monitoring report shows NZ is likely to meet the first emissions budget – but the second and third emissions budgets are at risk:

🟩 NZ is likely to meet the first emissions budget (2022–2025) – due in part to changes to accounting methods

🟧 There are significant risks to achieving the second emissions budget (2026–2030).

🟥 Current Government plans are insufficient to meet the third emissions budget (2031–2035).

🟧 There are significant risks for meeting the 2050 target.

Read the report and more info on our website: https://www.climatecommission.govt.nz/erm-2025?utm_source=youtube.com&utm_campaign=erm-2025&utm_medium=social&utm_content=short

Health care assistants care guide - our whakataukī and tohu

This video explains our approach to encompass both te ao Pākehā and te ao Māori views. This included the creation of taonga that resonate both to the kaupapa, and with everyone who has been involved in designing and implementing the guide.

A day in the life of a cyber security consultant

We chat with Kate who works with businesses to help keep them safe from cyber threats.  Kates talks us through a typical day, the most difficult challenges facing businesses when it comes to cyber security.  Also, how she stay's current with the rapidly evolving threat landscape and new technologies.

A career in cyber security at Kordia.

We chat to cyber security consultant Kate.  Originally a journalist, Kate discussed a passion for hacking during the covid pandemic.  We  find out what sparked her interest in this fast growing area, what training she did and what she loves most about working in cyber security at Kordia!

He Kete Mātauranga: Bringing Whenua Stories to Life

Nau mai, haere mai! This video is a recording of a special Ngā Poutama Matawhenua wānanga held on 13 June 2025.

Join Keith Holswich (Ngāti Rahiri, Te Atiawa, Taranaki) as he shares the powerful story of He Kete Mātauranga – a grassroots GIS system built by, for, and with hapū to protect, manage, and connect with their whenua.

In this session you’ll discover:
• How Ngāti Rahiri set up their own “kete” of digital whenua knowledge
• Real case studies of protecting wāhi tapu, supporting Takutai Moana claims, and working with councils and industry
• Why historic aerials, Māori Land Court data, and local mātauranga are the backbone of their GIS
• Keith’s practical tips, hard lessons, and ideas for any hapū, iwi, marae or Māori Land Trust wanting to start their own mapping kaupapa

This wānanga is for everyone: trustees, administrators, kaitiaki, planners, rangatahi, or anyone passionate about whenua, digital taonga, and mātauranga Māori. No tech skills needed – just an interest in learning how GIS can uplift your community and tell the real stories of your whenua.

Links:
